belgium.name: Spa-Francorchamps
belgium.text: Spa is high-deg: long high-speed corners (Eau Rouge, Pouhon, Blanchimont) put sustained energy through the tyres.

monaco.name: Monaco
monaco.text: Monaco is low-deg and overtaking-poor; track position dominates and a one-stop is the default unless a safety car appears.

netherlands.name: Zandvoort
netherlands.text: Zandvoort is medium-deg with banked corners; ARIS identity at lap 25 is Pit 33 HARD / Pit 30 HARD / Stay.

bahrain.name: Bahrain
bahrain.text: Bahrain is high-deg on rear tyres; two-stops are common and the undercut is usually powerful.

azerbaijan.name: Baku
azerbaijan.text: Baku is a high safety-car circuit: long straights, walls, and a historical SC rate of 1.0 in the ARIS 2022–2024 sample.

britain.name: Silverstone
britain.text: Silverstone is high-deg through fast corners (Copse, Maggotts, Becketts); ARIS often sees HARD as the long-stint tyre.

italy.name: Monza
italy.text: Monza is low-deg and low pit-loss relative to lap time; overcut can work because time on track is cheap.

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.text: Singapore is high-deg, high temperature, and street-circuit SC-prone; degradation plus traffic dominate strategy.

hungary.name: Hungaroring
hungary.text: Hungaroring is a high-downforce, overtaking-poor circuit where undercut value is large because of dirty air.

spain.name: Barcelona-Catalunya
spain.text: Spain is high-deg through long medium-speed corners; rear wear often decides whether a two-stop beats a one-stop.
